en.answer: The astronauts and the ISS are in free fall together. Although Earth's gravity is still strong at orbital altitude (~90% of surface strength), the astronauts, station, and all objects inside are accelerating toward Earth at the same rate due to that gravity. Weightlessness results from this shared free fall, not from the absence of gravity. An astronaut feels weight only when supported by a surface (a normal force); in orbit, there is no such force.
